text:
kevin: quick follow-up on the thin-proxy RFC — can we decide if we go multiplexed per-host proxy or keep per-tenant agents? need to lock this for Q3 capacity planning. pinging @maria @anya @sam

maria: +1 to decide. summary from last meeting: multiplexing reduces infra footprint but complicates per-tenant isolation and cert flows. per-tenant agents are simpler for audit/air-gapped customers.

anya: FWIW prototyped a multiplexing mode. micro-benchmarks below. results are noisy but indicative.
anya: perf notes: multiplex host proxy (1 host) handling 2000 concurrent streams -> p50 45ms, p95 180ms. per-tenant agent (same HW, 10 agents) -> p50 55ms, p95 210ms. multiplexing saved ~18% on p50 in our setup.

sam: interesting. did you test connection churn? iirc we saw head-of-line issues when many tenants reconnect at once.

anya: yeah churn matters. multiplexed proxy hit a limit on max active streams and we had to bump `max_streams`. reconnect storms cause short spikes in CPU and memory but recovered. per-tenant agents spread the reconnection cost.

sam: also think about cert rotation and key material: with multiplexing the host proxy needs to be able to present per-tenant certs or do SNI-based routing + backend auth. both add complexity.

maria: exactly — for compliance customers we currently require keys never leave customer network. per-tenant agent fits that. multiplexing would require either passthrough TLS (no termination) or per-tenant TLS contexts in the host proxy. both feasible but engineering cost is non-trivial.

kevin: what's the operational picture? fewer boxes to reason about vs one box that holds many tenant contexts. which one is easier on debugging?

anya: multiplexed is easier for resource planning (fewer processes), harder for single-tenant debugging (logs are co-mingled). we can add strong tracing headers and tenant ID tagging to logs to ease ops.

sam: from reliability POV per-tenant agents reduce blast radius. if agent crashes only that tenant is impacted. multiplex host proxy crash impacts many tenants. but we can run multiplex proxies in small pools per-region to reduce blast radius.

maria: cost tradeoff: initial estimate — multiplexing reduces instance count by ~30% at 10k tenants, but increases development + QA effort (we'd add ~3-4 engineer-months).

kevin: hybrid idea: default to multiplexed host proxies for self-serve tenants under threshold X, and require per-tenant agents for high-RPS or compliance tenants. this maps to Dedicated vs Private tiers. thoughts?

anya: we already saw that in perf. hybrid seems like low-friction: small tenants get cheaper infra, enterprise get isolation. rollout complexity is moderate (need onboarding flag + routing policy).

sam: agree. also suggest we add a lightweight 'ephemeral agent' mode — a minimal per-tenant sidecar that offloads certs and authorizations but funnels tokens through the host proxy. keeps keys local while leveraging multiplexing.

maria: ephemeral agent + host-proxy is interesting. implementation sketch: agent does mTLS with customer network, exchanges a short-lived attestation token, host proxy accepts token and routes by tenant. token lifetime ~5m, rotated by agent. preserves key locality.

sam: love that. need to evaluate failure modes: what if agent loses network? fallback to queued requests? we should define SLOs for agent connectivity and a graceful degrade path (reject vs fallback to dedicated endpoints).

kevin: actionable items: 1) @anya: run churn + token-rotation spike tests and share numbers (by EOW) 2) @maria: add cost/eng-effort delta vs per-tenant agents 3) @sam: draft failure-mode runbook and SLO thresholds. i'll write RFC addendum with hybrid + ephemeral-agent proposal after we get the numbers.

infra-bot: deploy check: test cluster with multiplex-proxy:v0.5 deployed to staging-eu at 1738205000 — no outages reported. :white_check_mark:

kevin: thanks all. if numbers look good we'll target hybrid in the next infra roadmap sync. :thumbsup:
